los.text: Identify rostral, caudal, dorsal, ventral, left and right on images of an axial CT brain, an axial MRI brain and an axial MRI spinal cord
los.html:
• Convention: axial CT and MRI are viewed from the feet, so the patient's left is on the viewer's right
    • the front of the patient is at the top of the image.
ImageTop of imageBottomOut of the plane
Axial brain (forebrain)Anterior = rostralPosterior = caudalDorsal (up) and ventral (down)
Axial spinal cordAnterior = ventralPosterior = dorsalRostral (up) and caudal (down)
  • Why the terms swap: the cephalic flexure bends the forebrain forward, so in the cerebrum dorsal = superior and rostral = anterior
    • in the brainstem and cord dorsal = posterior and rostral = superior.
TissueCTMRI T1MRI T2
BoneWhiteDark (marrow fat bright)Dark
CSFDarkDarkBright
Fresh bloodBrightVariesVaries
Grey vs white matterGrey slightly brighterWhite matter brighterGrey matter brighter
  • CT is first-line for stroke and head injury (fast, shows bleeding)
    • MRI shows the posterior fossa, cord and soft tissue better.

los.text: Identify the origins of the cranial nerves and identify their extra-cranial pathways to/from their effector/sensor structures and link to the functional outcomes of damage along those pathways
los.html:
NerveLeaves brainstemExits skullSuppliesDamage
I OlfactoryForebrain (olfactory bulb)Cribriform plateSmellAnosmia (head injury)
II OpticDiencephalonOptic canalVisionField defect depends on site
III OculomotorMidbrain, front (between peduncles)Superior orbital fissureMost eye muscles, levator palpebrae, pupil constrictionEye "down and out", ptosis, dilated pupil (PCom aneurysm, uncal herniation)
IV TrochlearMidbrain, back (only one)Superior orbital fissureSuperior obliqueVertical diplopia, worse going downstairs; head tilt
V TrigeminalPons, sideV1 SOF, V2 rotundum, V3 ovaleFace sensation, muscles of masticationNumb face, lost corneal reflex, jaw deviates to the weak side
VI AbducensPontomedullary junctionSOF (via cavernous sinus)Lateral rectusCan't abduct; horizontal diplopia; raised ICP (false localising sign)
VII FacialCerebellopontine angleInternal acoustic meatus → stylomastoid foramenFacial expression, taste (anterior 2/3), lacrimal and salivary glands, stapediusLMN: whole half of the face (Bell's); UMN: forehead spared
VIII VestibulocochlearCerebellopontine angleInternal acoustic meatusHearing, balanceDeafness, vertigo (vestibular schwannoma)
IX GlossopharyngealMedulla (behind olive)Jugular foramenTaste and sensation posterior 1/3 tongue, gag afferent, parotid, carotid sinusLost gag sensation
X VagusMedulla (behind olive)Jugular foramenPharynx, larynx, palate; parasympathetic to thorax and abdomenUvula deviates away from the lesion; hoarse voice
XI AccessorySpinal root C1–5Jugular foramenSCM, trapeziusWeak shrug and head turn
XII HypoglossalMedulla (between pyramid and olive)Hypoglossal canalTongue musclesTongue deviates towards the lesion

los.text: Identify the different structures in the brain stem (medulla, pons and midbrain), their relationships to each other and to the brain, spinal cord and other components of the posterior fossa, and link to the functional consequences of damage to these structures
los.html:
PartSurface featuresInsideCranial nerves
MidbrainCerebral peduncles (front), superior and inferior colliculi (back)Cerebral aqueduct, substantia nigra, red nucleusIII, IV
PonsBulging basilar part; basilar artery in front; middle cerebellar pedunclesFloor of the 4th ventricle behindV (side); VI, VII, VIII at its lower border
MedullaPyramids (decussate at the lower end), olivesLower 4th ventricle; cardiac and respiratory centresIX, X, XI, XII
  • Posterior fossa relations: clivus and basilar artery in front
    • cerebellum behind (4th ventricle between)
    • tentorium cerebelli above
    • foramen magnum below (medulla becomes the spinal cord).
LesionEffect
Lateral medullary (PICA, Wallenberg)Same-side face pain and temperature loss, opposite-side body loss, Horner's, dysphagia, ataxia, vertigo
Medial medullaryOpposite hemiparesis, tongue deviates to the lesion side
Locked-in (basilar artery, pons)Paralysed except vertical eye movements and blinking; aware
Weber's (midbrain)Same-side III palsy, opposite hemiparesis
Tonsillar herniation (coning)Medulla compressed in the foramen magnum → respiratory arrest
Uncal herniationIII compressed → fixed dilated pupil on the same side

los.text: Identify the main components of the cerebellum and its connection to the brain stem, spinal cord and cerebral hemispheres
los.html:
PartsTwo hemispheres joined by the midline vermis; anterior and posterior lobes (primary fissure); flocculonodular lobe (balance, eye movements).
Deep nuclei(lateral → medial)Dentate, emboliform, globose, fastigial ("Don't Eat Greasy Food").
PeduncleJoinsMain traffic
SuperiorMidbrainOutput from the dentate nucleus to the opposite thalamus (→ motor cortex) and red nucleus
Middle (largest)PonsInput from the opposite cerebral cortex via pontine nuclei
InferiorMedullaInput from the spinal cord (spinocerebellar), vestibular nuclei, inferior olive
FunctionCoordinates movement on the same side (double crossing).
Signs (DANISH)Dysdiadochokinesia, ataxia, nystagmus, intention tremor, slurred (scanning) speech, hypotonia.
LocalisingVermis (alcohol) → truncal ataxia and wide-based gait; hemisphere → same-side limb ataxia.

los.text: Recognise the grey and white matter of the brain, the internal capsule, cerebral peduncles, and primary motor cortex
los.html:
Grey matter
  • Cortex, basal ganglia, thalamus, brainstem nuclei (cell bodies).
  • White matter: tracts (myelinated axons)
  • on CT white matter is darker than grey.
Internal capsuleWhite matter between the caudate and thalamus (medial) and the lentiform nucleus (lateral): anterior limb, genu, posterior limb (corticospinal fibres to the limbs, sensory radiations).
Blood supplyLenticulostriate branches of the MCA; a small lacunar infarct here causes a dense opposite-side hemiplegia.
Primary motor cortexPrecentral gyrus (Brodmann 4); homunculus with the leg on the medial surface (ACA) and the arm and face laterally (MCA).
1. Corticospinal pathPrecentral gyrus → corona radiata → posterior limb of internal capsule.
2Cerebral peduncle (crus cerebri) in the midbrain.
3Basilar pons.
4Medullary pyramid, where ~85–90% decussate.
5. Lateral corticospinal tractAnterior horn cell.
